# Feature: Run-Local Sessions, Events & Audit

## 1. Feature Goal

**ID**: FEAT-023
**Source Plan**: `.spec-lite/plan_agentic.md`

Every agentic invocation produces exactly one self-contained, movable run directory: the run is created **before** provider/model/auth validation (so startup failures are auditable), the raw Pi session JSONL lives under `runs/<run-id>/agent/`, the manifest records session/model/prompt/tool metadata, tool lifecycle is projected into a stable `tool-calls.jsonl`, and usage is aggregated into `usage.json`. Audit/report code reads only the stable Yantra projection — never Pi internals.

## 2. Data Model (Granular)

Filesystem persistence (memory: no relational storage). Authoritative layout from plan §7:

```text
runs/<run-id>/
  manifest.json        # + new "agent" section (below)
  events.jsonl         # existing TaskEvent stream
  agent/
    <pi-session>.jsonl # canonical provider artifact (FEAT-022 places it)
  tool-calls.jsonl     # stable Yantra tool audit projection (new)
  usage.json           # aggregated usage (existing writer, new agent source)
  confirmations.jsonl  # confirmation decisions (existing gateway artifact)
  secrets.jsonl        # secret resolution references (existing)
  captures/  brief.*  report.md
```

### Entities & Attributes

- **Manifest `agent` section** (JSON object inside `manifest.json`):
  - `adapter` (string) — `"pi-coding-agent"`.
  - `sdk_version` (string) — resolved at runtime from the installed package.
  - `provider` / `model` / `thinking` (strings) — effective model selection.
  - `auth_source` (`"managed" | "runtime-key" | "environment"`) — credential origin (never the credential).
  - `session_id` (string), `session_file` (string, **relative** path) — run dirs stay movable.
  - `prompt_version` (string, `"agent-v1"`), `prompt_hash` (sha256 of prompt text), `tool_catalog_hash` (sha256 over canonical name+schema+description serialization).
- **ToolAuditEntry** (one JSONL line in `tool-calls.jsonl`; exact shape from plan §7):
  - `ts` (ISO-8601 UTC), `seq` (number, monotonic per run), `run_id`, `session_id`, `call_id`, `tool` (strings).
  - `phase` (`'start' | 'end'`), `input_sanitized?` / `output_sanitized?` (unknown, post-sanitizer only).
  - `status?` (`'ok' | 'error' | 'denied' | 'aborted'`), `duration_ms?`, `error_code?`, `confirmation_id?`.
- **usage.json agent fields**: `turns`, `input_tokens?`, `output_tokens?`, `cost_usd?` merged into the existing usage document.

### Relationships

- 1 run : 1 agent session (fresh session per run, plan §14.4); `manifest.agent.session_file` → the JSONL under `agent/`.
- 1 `tool_started` `AgentEvent` : 1 `start` entry : 0..1 `end` entry (missing `end` = incomplete call, must render as such).
- `confirmation_id` joins a ToolAuditEntry to `confirmations.jsonl`.

### Indexes & Constraints

- `seq` strictly monotonic within a run; writer is the single owner of the counter.
- Zod schemas for the manifest agent section and ToolAuditEntry live in `packages/protocol` (schema-as-source-of-truth per memory).
- The legacy full request/response `agent.jsonl` is **not** written by this path (plan §7).

- [ ] **Unit Tests**: Schema round-trip valid/invalid cases: bad `phase`, non-ISO `ts`, negative `seq`, absolute `session_file` rejected (must be relative), unknown keys rejected (closed schemas).

### TASK-002: Run-first lifecycle — create before validate, finalize failed startups

- [ ] **Implementation**: Extend the run store so agentic commands create the run directory + initial manifest **before** any provider/model/auth resolution. Add `finalizeStartupFailure(runId, agentError)`: writes the typed error into the manifest, emits `task_failed` to `events.jsonl`, writes `report.md`, sets terminal state. Partial `agent` manifest data (whatever was resolved before the failure) is retained.
- [ ] **Unit Tests**: (a) startup failure (e.g. `AGENT_AUTH_UNAVAILABLE`) leaves a complete, auditable run dir: manifest with error, `report.md`, `task_failed` event; (b) exit-code mapping per memory (2 = execution failure); (c) run dir is created exactly once (no orphan second dir on retry).
- [ ] **Documentation Update**: `docs/` run-artifacts page: "failed startups are runs too" behavior.
- **Verify**: Manual: run `yantra do "x"` with no credentials → `yantra audit <run-id>` renders the typed failure.
- **Depends on**: TASK-001

### TASK-004: `tool-calls.jsonl` projection writer

- [ ] **Implementation**: `tool-call-writer.ts` — append-only JSONL writer owning the monotonic `seq`; `run-recorder.ts` maps seam `tool_started` → `phase:'start'` entry and `tool_finished` → `phase:'end'` entry (status from `isError`/middleware outcome, `duration_ms` computed, `confirmation_id` threaded when the middleware supplies one — FEAT-024). Writer is crash-safe: every line flushed; `close()` idempotent; process-termination leaves at worst a missing `end` (never a torn line — write each line atomically).
- [ ] **Unit Tests**: (a) start/end pairing and monotonic seq under interleaved async completions (tool B ends before tool A); (b) aborted run leaves valid JSONL with identifiable incomplete calls; (c) property test: any sequence of seam events serializes to lines that all parse against the ToolAuditEntry schema; (d) inputs/outputs in entries are the sanitized payloads (plant canary in fake event; assert redacted form only).
- [ ] **Documentation Update**: run-artifacts docs: `tool-calls.jsonl` format and its stability guarantee vs the raw Pi session.
- **Verify**: Chaos test (kill mid-run in a child-process test) yields parseable `tool-calls.jsonl`.
- **Depends on**: TASK-003

## 6. Cross-Cutting Concerns

- **Auth**: N/A directly; records `auth_source` metadata only — never credential material (canary-tested).
- **Error Handling**: startup failures finalize as auditable runs (plan §9); all writers use `Result`/typed errors; no `process.exit(0)` on error.
- **Logging**: run dir is the canonical observability artifact; pino `info` for run lifecycle, `debug` for writer activity. Tests inspect events/artifacts, not logs.
- **Security**: `tool-calls.jsonl` carries only post-sanitizer payloads; raw Pi session inherits restrictive run-dir permissions (plan §8.10); secret-canary scan over every produced file is part of this feature's suite.
